items.title: Two oil tankers ablaze after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Two oil tankers ablaze after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps said two oil tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz had struck naval mines. In a statement to the ISNA news agency, the IRGC said: "two oil tankers travelling in the southern no-go zone of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a massive explosion after hitting sea mines." Both tankers were reportedly set ablaze after the blast. ISNA added that one of the supertankers carried more than two million barrels of crude oil, whcih sank in the southern waters of the Gulf.

items.title: Iran's navy says three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.summary: Nov 14 (Reuters) - Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. One tanker hit a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, while two others struck mines later in the day. "Two violating tankers ... were attempting to slip through a prohibited route in the Strait of Hormuz when they hit naval mines, exploded, and burst into flames," Iran's IRNA news agency quoted the Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying about the evening incident.

items.title: Iran’s IRGC says two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran’s IRGC says two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz Two oil tankers struck naval mines as they tried to cross the Strait of Hormuz “secretly”, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy says. In a statement published by Iran’s state news agency IRNA, the navy said the ships switched off their tracking and navigation equipment and took an “unauthorised” route. “Following the explosions of these two tankers, two other tankers that were attempting to transit secretly complied with the warnings from the Naval Force’s traffic control centre in the Strait of Hormuz and returned towards the waters of the Persian Gulf,” the IRGC said.

items.title: Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz: Iran's navy
items.summary: Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz: Iran's navy Iran’s navy said a second oil tanker caught fire on Saturday morning after hitting a naval mine while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media. “Fire and explosions are the fate of tankers involved in illegal activities that have turned off their tracking systems and are operating in restricted areas,” the navy said, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. The navy did not identify the vessel. It was the fifth oil tanker in 24 hours to catch fire after reportedly being struck by Iranian forces or hitting a naval mine while attempting to transit the strait.

"A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorised route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine," the Guards' navy said in a statement on the incident in the south of the waterway, carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday. A separate statement from Iran's conventional navy said another tanker "navigating through the unsafe and prohibited zone east of the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking and identification systems switched off, caught fire and was forced to stop after striking a naval mine". The statements did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but the Guards said one of those hit in south Hormuz was a supertanker. The prospects for any grand bargain emerging from the rare encounter, however, are slim.

items.summary: Trump to discuss Iran war, but not Ukraine, at China summit US President Donald Trump will discuss the Iran war with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week but he is not expected to discuss Ukraine war, a US official said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. "The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," Wales said. "I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin," a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call. items.summary: Nov 13 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump will hold a trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the annual APEC conference in Shenzhen on Thursday, the New York Post reported on Friday. The trilateral discussion is expected to focus largely on developing an ambitious nuclear arms control pact, but discussions could also touch on North Korea and the Iran war, the Post reported. Trump has already publicly indicated that he planned to meet with the two leaders.

items.title: Trump says US military action against Iran not necessary 'at this point'
items.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump on Monday told reporters that military action by the United States against Iran did not currently seem necessary. "At this point ... taking the military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing. But we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes," Trump told reporters. "I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," he said, referring to the conflict against Tehran. (Reporting by Steve Holland, writing by Bhargav Acharya;Editing by David Ljunggren)

WSJ: Iran still has 1,500-2,500 missiles, influencing US plans for renewed war
items.summary: WSJ: Iran still has 1,500-2,500 missiles, influencing US plans for renewed war American intelligence believes that Iran has some 1,500-2,500 missiles, and the apparent size of the arsenal has impacted Trump administration's decision on whether to resume strikes on the Islamic Republic, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing officials. The officials told the newspaper that it is a “low confidence assessment” given the difficulties in tracking Tehran’s munitions, but that it was clear that the regime still possessed a large number of missiles. The report says Israeli officials believe Tehran has over 1,500 ballistic missiles. On Friday, Deputy Commander of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps Major General Mostafa Izadi, said Iranian forces were capable of launching missiles equipped with two-ton warheads at targets 1,500 kilometres away. Last Saturday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it has lifted its self-imposed 2,000km limit on the range of its ballistic missiles.

items.summary: BASRA, Iraq, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Iraq barred a plane carrying Iran's national soccer team from landing at Basra airport on Tuesday, a decision by the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority linked to US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines, two Basra airport officials said. The plane returned to Iran and landed at Abadan airport, and the team will now travel overland to Basra, an Iranian consulate official in Basra said. The Iranian team was travelling to Iraq to participate in a four-nation tournament in Basra also involving Iraq, Lebanon and Palestine.

items.summary: US military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman A US military aircraft fired on and disabled a commercial vessel that tried to break the US naval blockade of Iran on Saturday, US Central Command (Centcom) said. The St Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo ship had visited an Iranian port and was trying to leave regional waters when a US plane fired precision munitions at its stern, after US forces ordered the crew to clear the targeted areas of the vessel, Centcom said. The US military also said on Saturday it was launching a task force to crack down on Iran’s movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material across its land borders and through the Caspian Sea, expanding on its months-long naval blockade. Centcom estimated that the blockade had prevented Iran from exporting more than $25bn worth of crude oil.

Woorden van die strekking liepen drie jaar geleden nog uit op een felle strijd, maar voorzitter Australië probeert het nu toch weer. Landen hebben vanaf nu de kans om te reageren op de tekst, waarmee eind deze week de klimaattop wordt afgesloten. De passages zouden dus nog aangepast of geschrapt kunnen worden. Unable to win over Ankara, Europe should drop its objections to Tbilisi to avert a crisis. With three weeks to go until the OSCE Ministerial Council in Lugano, Switzerland, on December 3, the organization remains deadlocked over who should lead it from 2027-28. The chairperson-in-office role rotates every two years and is normally voted on well in advance with agreement by consensus. EU member Cyprus was the first country to put its hat in the ring almost two years ago, in December 2024. clusters.headline: A Second Path Under the Caspian: What the Trans-Caspian Cable Changes for Eurasian Connectivity

items.title: A Second Path Under the Caspian: What the Trans-Caspian Cable Changes for Eurasian Connectivity
items.summary: When the presidents of Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan inaugurated a 380-kilometer fiber-optic cable beneath the Caspian Sea on October 15, they opened the first fiber-optic link across the Caspian seabed. Designed for a capacity of at least 400 terabits per second, the cable matters chiefly because it creates an alternative: data moving between Central Asia and Europe can now take a westbound route that avoids Russian networks. Kazakhstan gains an additional international connection, and Azerbaijan strengthens its role as a transit hub. Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, which depend on Kazakhstan for international connectivity, stand to gain indirectly, and carriers and cloud providers gain another potential route between Asia and Europe. How far these gains extend will depend on how much traffic the link comes to carry.

clusters.headline: En Auschwitz con el heredero del Sah de Irán para apoyar a los judíos

items.title: En Auschwitz con el heredero del Sah de Irán para apoyar a los judíos
items.summary: En fila india, en silencio y tiritando de frío, nuestras sombras avanzan por un túnel oscuro camino del matadero. A través de ese pasaje subterráneo en el que suenan los nombres de los judíos que aquí fueron exterminados, la visita al campo de concentración de Auschwitz sobrecoge desde la entrada, incluso antes de llegar a la puerta de hierro con su infame cartel 'El trabajo os hará libre' ('ARBEIT MACHT FREI', escrito en alemán en mayúsculas). Cuentan que la B de 'ARBEIT' ('trabajo') está al revés, más ancha por arriba que por abajo, porque así la puso un herrero polaco preso en el campo, Jan Liwacz, como pequeño gesto de rebeldía para demostrar la falsedad del eslogan: aquí nada traía la libertad, solo la muerte.Se calcula que en el campo de Auschwitz y en el de Birkenau, a tres kilómetros y medio, perecieron un millón de los seis millones de judíos que los nazis mataron en el Holocausto durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial (1939-45). Sus instalaciones, convertidas en un museo para que no se olvide aquel horror, reciben cada año dos millones de visitantes, muchos de ellas ilustres.Coi

Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes and winding down hostilities, and current and former officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind about how to resolve the unpopular conflict, which he launched in February with Israel. But in meetings with his national security advisers and after a series of intelligence briefings, Trump said he was considering holding off on strikes, said the people, who, like others interviewed for this story, spoke on condition of anonymity. He has also indicated sympathy for allies in the region who have asked him not to return to a full-fledged war. The visit comes as the Israeli prime minister is pressing President Trump to resume the war against Iran. Axios said Gofman was to meet CIA Director John Ratcliffe and later expected to travel to Miami to meet White House envoy Steve Witkoff. Mossad, the CIA and the White House declined to comment, Axios said. Meanwhile Israel's Channel 12 news reported that Gofman’s trip was not disclosed to Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot in his Thursday security briefing with Netanyahu. items.summary: Het Witte Huis meldt dat er volgende week een uniek topoverleg is tussen de leiders van de VS, China en Rusland. Dat werd vannacht door de Amerikaanse regering aan journalisten meegedeeld. De Chinese regering heeft het driepartijenoverleg niet bevestigd. Als dat overleg er komt, is het de eerste keer dat de leiders van die landen elkaar samen spreken. De ontmoeting zou plaatsvinden te midden van de Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) in de Chinese stad Shenzhen en zou onder meer gaan over het verminderen van kernwapens. "President Trump is van mening dat de uitbreiding van kernwapens zeer gevaarlijk is", zei woordvoerder Olivia Wales van het Witte Huis tegen verslaggevers. Het laatste kernwapenverdrag tussen de VS en Rusland liep in februari af. Anonieme analisten zeggen tegen de Amerikaanse pers dat ze geen nieuw akkoord verwachten. "Ik zou dit omschrijven als het startpunt, het eerste gesprek op het niveau van deze leiders tussen de landen", zegt een functionaris tegen CNN. items.summary: US says it shot down two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain The US military on Friday said it had shot down two Iranian attack drones launched towards Bahrain, denying an Iranian claim that its forces had struck a US early-warning radar system in the Gulf kingdom. US Central Command (Centcom) said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain, both of which were intercepted by US forces. Centcom also rejected the IRGC’s claim that it had attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain earlier in the day. The competing accounts come amid questions from some US lawmakers about the Pentagon’s disclosure of details surrounding incidents in the conflict, while scepticism has also circulated on social media.

items.title: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise
items.summary: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise US President Donald Trump has extended by 90 days a waiver of a shipping law so that foreign-flagged ships can transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday. The administration would extend the waiver of the more than 100-year-old Jones Act, Reuters reported, citing industry sources. The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched its war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. When it extended the waiver in August, it said it would decide cases on a case-by-case basis, a condition that also applies to the latest extension. The Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies, and crewed by American workers. The waiver aims to lower gasoline, diesel, and fertiliser prices, which have risen because of the war. clusters.headline: Snoh Aalegra: Legendary Love review – raw R&B talent restrained by reverence for the greats

items.title: Snoh Aalegra: Legendary Love review – raw R&B talent restrained by reverence for the greats
items.summary: (Stem) Her truly remarkable, Sade-ish voice is hypnotic against some dizzyingly plush production, but a modern spin on 80s pastiche sometimes veers too close to tribute Swedish-Iranian singer Snoh Aalegra has previously described her music – a lush, pastiche-y mix of R&B, hip-hop, soul and pop – as “cinematic soul”. But although she’s a dab hand at graceful, timeless presentation (and has a truly remarkable voice) Aalegra’s music has often struggled to match up to its aesthetic, hampered by her love of the greats and a penchant for broadly generic lyrics. Her most recent album, 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies , made some headway toward carving out a more distinctive sound, thanks to sparky and inventive production from Tyler, the Creator, No ID, P2J and the Neptunes, but still didn’t quite feel like the right fit. items.summary: Order a Diet Coke or invade Iran – that’s the choice facing the US president in one of several satirical games, as designers turn the gamification of politics back on the White House In early September, the Trump White House announced a surprising new addition to its official website. Named simply Arcade , it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia. The US president hoped the creator of Power Slap, a face-slapping league which one of the world’s leading neurologists called “a sport inconsistent with the intelligence of humans”, might be the right man to deliver his daily rebuttals to the media. Trump later backtracked on the appointment, saying he was “only kidding” , yet it is easy to understand why he might be pining for White’s muscles, trash talk and thirst for athletic violence. White is representative of the way Trump transcended politics in 2024 to become a celebrated figure in the manosphere, the loosely defined cluster of male content creators who have a direct line to America’s bored and aggrieved young men. In a note to clients, Bank of America said Saudi Arabia is grappling with “contagion” caused by liquidity tightness in the UAE and a rapid slowdown in the kingdom’s own economy, according to an article published on Bloomberg on Tuesday. The report said Saudi banks are feeling the pain in the UAE, which is also grappling with fallout from the Iran war and tighter liquidity. Saudi banks are closely linked to their Emirati neighbours, with a high number of interbank transactions contributing to deposits at Saudi banks. At the same time, the Saudi economy is under strain and government entities are making withdrawals from Saudi banks. But loan demand is high, which is effectively raising the cost of Saudi money. items.summary: Op de klimaattop in Turkije was het een komen en gaan van wereldleiders. In het geval van premier Jetten was het de nationale politiek die zijn inbreng op de top kleurde: hij bleef geheel weg uit Antalya vanwege de problemen die hij thuis heeft met het belastingplan . Grote afwezigen, naast Jetten, waren de Amerikaanse president Trump, de Indiase premier Modi en de Chinese president Xi, al stuurde die laatste wel een vertegenwoordiger. Van de wereldleiders die wel gingen, trok de Braziliaanse president Lula veel bekijks. Zijn aanwezigheid is voor veel aanwezigen op de klimaattop een onuitgesproken opluchting. clusters.headline: Iran, la base segreta è nascosta sottoterra: ecco com'è fatta la "città dei missili" dei Pasdaran

items.title: Iran, la base segreta è nascosta sottoterra: ecco com'è fatta la "città dei missili" dei Pasdaran
items.summary: L'Iran ha svelato una nuova base missilistica segreta sotterranea dei Guardiani della Rivoluzione: come si vede nelle immagini diffuse dalla televisione di Stato IRIB, la struttura ospiterebbe missili balistici a propellente solido e liquido, missili da crociera e sistemi di lancio. items.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. As the GOP scrambles to repair the damage and Democrats strategize about how to use their new power in a divided Washington, one takeaway seems obvious: this was a foreign policy election, in which the Iran war and the costs it brought home served as the tipping point. What does JD Vance's day-after effort to distance himself from the war tell us about how Republicans are digesting this result? clusters.headline: Israeli nuclear weapons, 2026

items.title: Israeli nuclear weapons, 2026
items.summary: Israel's longstanding policy of nuclear ambiguity ("amimut"), combined with severe intelligence restrictions and historical deception, continues to obscure the exact details of its undeclared nuclear arsenal. Despite these open-source research challenges, technical assessments suggest Israel maintains a strategic stockpile of roughly 90 single-stage, boosted fission warheads. This force is deployable across a triad of air, land, and sea delivery systems—including F-15/F-16/F-35 aircraft, Jericho ballistic missiles, and modified Dolphin-class submarines—even as US policy faces mounting domestic political pressure to abandon its decades-long refusal to acknowledge Israel's nuclear capability.

items.title: Qatar says US and Iran have responded positively to mediation
items.summary: Qatar says US and Iran have responded positively to mediation Qatar says Washington and Tehran have both responded positively to efforts to mediate between them. Doha is “working tirelessly to end the uncertainty over the crisis between Washington and Tehran”, the Qatari Foreign Ministry said. At his weekly briefing, the ministry’s media and communications director, Ibrahim bin Sultan al-Hashmi, said mediation was continuing. He added that the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the onset of winter were doubling the cost of the crisis. Al-Hashmi also condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and said Qatar backed all steps Riyadh took to protect its security and stability.

clusters.headline: Cuts, evictions, and job losses: A view from the trenches of climate science in 2026

items.title: Cuts, evictions, and job losses: A view from the trenches of climate science in 2026
items.summary: A researcher at Columbia University who studies atmospheric and climate science gives a first-hand account of what it is like to pursue this work in the Trump 2.0 era, when the foundations of American science are being profoundly shaken. The post-World War II traditions that have made American science so successful—generous funding, awarded based on merit via peer review; academic freedom; openness to foreign talent; and most of all, systems of funding and executing science that are largely run by scientists, rather than by politicians—are under siege. What comes next is still an open question.

clusters.headline: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security

items.title: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security
items.summary: Water, energy, and mineral resources have long played a role in influencing and inciting political, ideological, and economic violence. But this violence is now worsening, driven by growing population pressures, expanding economies, and a fracturing and reforming of political alliances — and the wars in Ukraine, Israel-Palestine, and Iran. One surprising result may be an unanticipated acceleration of the global transition away from fossil fuels.

items.summary: Although Donald Trump’s rejection of climate science has been embraced by many Australian conservatives, it has had limited impact on Canberra’s climate and energy agenda. In Australia, corporate attention on climate was already waning even before the second Trump election victory—something which was also true on a global level. So was media coverage, and public opinion. But Trump has legitimized and encouraged backsliding.

clusters.headline: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality

items.title: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality
items.summary: The historian Stephen Kotkin of Stanford’s Hoover Institution has penned an important new essay on the phenomenon of “junk history”: reductionist or plainly wrong interpretations of historical events that have little or no basis in empirical reality but are nevertheless “marshaled in policy debates as justification for action, up to launching wars.” The emblematic example, which has recently been used by advocates for the war with Iran, is the failure of British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain to truly ensure “peace in our time” at Munich in 1938. As Kotkin once put it, “It turns out not everything is Munich. It turns out Munich wasn’t even Munich when you get down into the nitty-gritty details.” Another example of junk history is what many otherwise well-informed American observers think they know about Sweden’s conduct during World War II and the Cold War. items.summary: Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz after mine collision Iran's navy reports that an oil tanker caught fire after colliding with a naval mine while travelling through a "prohibited" area in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. According to the reports, the vessel turned off its navigation systems and ignored “regular warnings”. No casualties have been reported. The navy subsequently issued a warning to other ships attempting to cross the contested waterway without Iranian permission. “This is the fate of all ships and vessels that ignore warnings and travel in prohibited areas,” it said in comments carried by Iran’s semi-official broadcaster IRIB.

Mohebbi said Washington had previously predicted that Iran would suffer economic collapse within two weeks, but that this had not happened. Tehran had prepared for economic pressure and maintained close relations with neighbouring countries, he said. items.summary: In Saudi-Arabië is een gebouw van het staatsoliebedrijf Aramco beschadigd geraakt door vallend puin na een verijdelde aanval. Op beelden is te zien dat op meerdere verdiepingen ramen zijn gesneuveld. Ook de gevel raakte beschadigd. Het gebouw is een van de hoogste in het financiële district van de Saudische hoofdstad Riyad. Volgens het ministerie van Energie is de schade beperkt gebleven. Eerder meldden de Saudiërs dat ze twee raketten hadden onderschept die vanuit Jemen op Riyad waren afgevuurd door de Houthi's. Mogelijk is het Aramco-gebouw beschadigd door brokstukken van de twee projectielen. Ook werden meerdere harde explosies gehoord in de stad. Daarnaast zijn kruisraketten onderschept en vernietigd in het zuiden van Saudi-Arabië. In Jemen woedt sinds 2014 een burgeroorlog tussen de Houthi's , die worden gesteund door Iran, en het Jemenitische regeringsleger, dat wordt gesteund door Saudi-Arabië. items.title: Iran executeert drie mannen voor onder meer brandstichting bij protesten
items.summary: In Iran zijn drie mannen geëxecuteerd voor hun rol bij anti-regime-protesten in Karaj, een stad ten westen van Teheran. Dat meldt staatspersbureau IRNA. De protesten kwamen begin dit jaar tot een kookpunt. Om deze een halt toe te brengen, richtten Iraanse autoriteiten en paramilitairen een bloedbad aan onder demonstranten. Naar schatting ruim 7000 betogers werden gedood , ook werden duizenden actievoerders vastgezet. De drie geëxecuteerde mannen, Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi en Reza Zanganeh, hebben volgens Iraanse autoriteiten vuurwapens, granaten en molotovcocktails gebruikt bij demonstraties op 8 en 9 januari. Ze zouden brand hebben gesticht bij openbare voorzieningen en een elektriciteitsstation hebben beschadigd, wat tot stroomuitval in sommige gebieden zou hebben geleid. De mannen werden er ook van beschuldigd dat zij opdrachten uitvoerden voor Israël en de Verenigde Staten, aartsvijanden van Iran. People in the many countries that suffered pain, loss and cruel indignities at the hands of Donald Trump over the past two chaotic, fearful years celebrated a moment of glorious, shared redemption. The monster, like others of his kind, still lurks in his gilded White House lair; far-right authoritarianism still casts a dark shadow over many nations. But the power of this most destructive of presidents is shattered , his malignant spell broken. clusters.headline: Corporate Re-entry as an Indicator of the End of the “Age of Wars”

items.title: Corporate Re-entry as an Indicator of the End of the “Age of Wars”
items.summary: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 marked not only a military but also an economic turning point in the international order. The mass withdrawal of multinational corporations (MNCs) from Russia demonstrated that geopolitical risk had begun to outweigh the benefits of global economic interdependence. But if corporate exit is one indicator of the beginning of a new “age of wars”, the gradual return of MNCs could be an indicator of its eventual end. Corporate return should not, however, be measured as a binary variable of returned/not returned. It is better understood as a sequence of increasingly costly and difficult-to-reverse commitments. This paper proposes a “corporate re-entry ladder” ranging from renewed institutional contacts and market reconnaissance to direct commercial presence and, ultimately, irreversible capital investment. clusters.headline: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers

items.title: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers
items.summary: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers The United States Central Command (Centcom) has directed the establishment of a task force that will support US government's efforts to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials. In a statement issued on Saturday on X, Centcom said Admiral Brad Cooper has directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, an internal staff of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with other US government agencies on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and "illegal revenue streams" across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, Centcom added. "The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," said Cooper. "Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with U.S. inter-agency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military." https://t.co/xUcO5

items.title: Oppositieleider Eisenkot mag Israëlische regering vormen, maar staat voor lastige puzzel
items.summary: In Israël mag oppositieleider Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) als eerste proberen om een nieuwe regering te vormen. President Herzog heeft hem aangewezen als eerste formateur. De Likud-partij van Netanyahu was bij de verkiezingen dan wel de grootste, maar Eisenkot kreeg meer aanbevelingen van de partijen. Er zijn meerdere wegen die naar een regering kunnen leiden, maar eenvoudig wordt het niet. De Arabische partijen - de Verenigde Arabische Lijst (Ra'am) en de Gezamenlijke Lijst - hebben deze verkiezingen een recordaantal van negentien zetels gehaald. Zij kunnen Eisenkot aan een regering helpen, maar meerdere leiders uit het oppositieblok sluiten zo'n samenwerking uit. Vier voorwaarden Eisenkot zelf zegt met iedereen te kunnen samenwerken die aan zijn vier voorwaarden voldoet: het erkennen van Israël als Joodse en democratische staat, het onderschrijven van de waarden van de onafhankelijkheidsverklaring, militaire of maatschappelijke dienstplicht voor iedereen, erkennen dat Hamas een terreurorganisatie is en toezeggen om de militaire en bestuurlijke capaciteit van de groep te ontmantelen. clusters.headline: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles

items.title: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles
items.summary: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards has said that it has lifted restrictions on the range of Iran's missiles. IRGC spokesman, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi reportedly made the comments at a press conference on Saturday, in response to question regarding the country's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei's warning to the US against further attacks on the country. Khamenei had previously said during a meeting with senior military commanders, that any renewed US or Israeli attck would be met with "with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response". The leader also reportedly ordered an update of Iran's military target database. According to Tasnim news agency, Mohebbi was asked on Saturday whether Khamenei's comments meant that limits on the range of Iranian missiles had been removed. He responded : "This restriction has been lifted for us". “Our duty is to show our capabilities on the battlefield,” he added.

clusters.headline: Voormalig Midden-Oostencorrespondent Thomas Loudon (56) overleden

items.title: Voormalig Midden-Oostencorrespondent Thomas Loudon (56) overleden
items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. Ook richtte hij zijn eigen organisatie op om journalisten te ondersteunen in landen waar de persvrijheid onder druk staat. Daa

Yet the reactions also expose the contradictions of the European Union’s own foreign policy, particularly toward the wars in Iran and Ukraine. items.title: Freezer meltdowns and airline hoaxes are a taste of things to come. Hoping for the best is no longer an option | Elisabeth Braw
items.summary: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . items.title: Squabble over leadership risks plunging the OSCE into crisis
items.summary: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) is staring down the barrel of entering 2027 without a chair for the first time in its 51-year history. The Europeans are wrestling Turkey to drop its veto over Cyprus’ bid, raising the stakes by loudly opposing the only other candidate, Georgia. Unable to win over Ankara, Europe should drop its objections to Tbilisi to avert a crisis. With three weeks to go until the OSCE Ministerial Council in Lugano, Switzerland, on December 3, the organization remains deadlocked over who should lead it from 2027-28. The chairperson-in-office role rotates every two years and is normally voted on well in advance with agreement by consensus. EU member Cyprus was the first country to put its hat in the ring almost two years ago, in December 2024. However, Cyprus’ bid has been vetoed by Turkey on the basis of the long-standing dispute over the division of the island in 1974 . items.title: Trump's Africa envoy puts on a masterclass in bad diplomacy
items.summary: Since returning to the White House, President Donald Trump has increasingly relied on special envoys to deal with some of his most vexing foreign policy challenges. While Trump slashed the use of special envoys in his first term, he has come around in his second term, in part because they allow him to bypass his career foreign service officers by compartmentalizing information from “deep state bureaucrats” who he has accused of spying on him and leaking his dealmaking to the press. As in previous administrations, the current Trump administration has assembled a collection of envoys largely based on region and policy imperative. Regions like the Middle East, South and Central Asia, and the Arctic all have special envoys, as do specific countries like Syria, Belarus, Greenland, and Ukraine (currently vacant). Similarly high-profile or strategic policy objectives like hostage affairs and combating anti-Semitism also have designated special envoys. items.title: A Second Path Under the Caspian: What the Trans-Caspian Cable Changes for Eurasian Connectivity
items.summary: When the presidents of Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan inaugurated a 380-kilometer fiber-optic cable beneath the Caspian Sea on October 15, they opened the first fiber-optic link across the Caspian seabed. Designed for a capacity of at least 400 terabits per second, the cable matters chiefly because it creates an alternative: data moving between Central Asia and Europe can now take a westbound route that avoids Russian networks. Kazakhstan gains an additional international connection, and Azerbaijan strengthens its role as a transit hub. Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, which depend on Kazakhstan for international connectivity, stand to gain indirectly, and carriers and cloud providers gain another potential route between Asia and Europe. How far these gains extend will depend on how much traffic the link comes to carry.

items.title: Jordan condemns Iranian drone strike on Bahrain
items.summary: Jordan condemns Iranian drone strike on Bahrain Jordan joined other regional partners in condemning Iran’s targeting of Bahrain amid uncertainty over whether the war involving Iran, the United States and Israel would continue. A Jordanian foreign ministry spokesperson described the attacks as a “dangerous escalation and a blatant breach of international law”. The spokesperson condemned “Iran’s brutal attacks on the sister kingdom of Bahrain” as a violation of its sovereignty and a threat to its security, stability and territorial integrity.

items.title: IRGC says Bahrain drone strike responded to ‘US aggression’ in southern Iran
items.summary: IRGC says Bahrain drone strike responded to ‘US aggression’ in southern Iran Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had launched a drone strike on a US airbase in Bahrain in response to an American attack on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran. Speaking to Sepah News, an IRGC spokesperson said the force had used “six drones” to target “the radar of the US defence site at the al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain”. “Expensive American drones are being shot down one after another, and a greater number of IRGC drones are heading towards American targets at this stage than in the previous stage, so the enemy knows any aggression will result in a tough and calculated response,” the spokesperson said.

items.title: Global diesel prices ease as winter approaches
items.summary: Global diesel prices, which have remained elevated since the start of the Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have fallen sharply in recent weeks as Gulf exports recover and global oil supplies get back on track for the first time since February. The price drop is being felt in Europe, where prices remain roughly 77% above pre-war levels, and in the US, where the national average fell below $6 a gallon on Saturday. Details by Liza Kaminov.

items.title: Yemen government forces withdraw from area near Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Houthis in control
items.summary: Nov 15 (Reuters) - Yemeni forces fighting for the internationally recognised Saudi-backed government said on Sunday that they were withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Iran-aligned Houthis in control. The government's retreat from the Bab el-Mandeb area hands the Houthis greater leverage over the maritime chokepoint, creating a potent pressure point on global shipping while Iran continues to disrupt traffic through the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.

items.title: Yemeni government force retreats from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
items.summary: By Mohammed Ghobari Nov 15 (Reuters) - Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis. The announcement signalled the apparent end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that squeezed oil exports.

items.title: En Auschwitz con el heredero del Sah de Irán para apoyar a los judíos
items.summary: En fila india, en silencio y tiritando de frío, nuestras sombras avanzan por un túnel oscuro camino del matadero. A través de ese pasaje subterráneo en el que suenan los nombres de los judíos que aquí fueron exterminados, la visita al campo de concentración de Auschwitz sobrecoge desde la entrada, incluso antes de llegar a la puerta de hierro con su infame cartel 'El trabajo os hará libre' ('ARBEIT MACHT FREI', escrito en alemán en mayúsculas). Cuentan que la B de 'ARBEIT' ('trabajo') está al revés, más ancha por arriba que por abajo, porque así la puso un herrero polaco preso en el campo, Jan Liwacz, como pequeño gesto de rebeldía para demostrar la falsedad del eslogan: aquí nada traía la libertad, solo la muerte.Se calcula que en el campo de Auschwitz y en el de Birkenau, a tres kilómetros y medio, perecieron un millón de los seis millones de judíos que los nazis mataron en el Holocausto durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial (1939-45). Sus instalaciones, convertidas en un museo para que no se olvide aquel horror, reciben cada año dos millones de visitantes, muchos de ellas ilustres.Coi

WSJ: Iran still has 1,500-2,500 missiles, influencing US plans for renewed war
items.summary: WSJ: Iran still has 1,500-2,500 missiles, influencing US plans for renewed war American intelligence believes that Iran has some 1,500-2,500 missiles, and the apparent size of the arsenal has impacted Trump administration's decision on whether to resume strikes on the Islamic Republic, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing officials. The officials told the newspaper that it is a “low confidence assessment” given the difficulties in tracking Tehran’s munitions, but that it was clear that the regime still possessed a large number of missiles. The report says Israeli officials believe Tehran has over 1,500 ballistic missiles. On Friday, Deputy Commander of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps Major General Mostafa Izadi, said Iranian forces were capable of launching missiles equipped with two-ton warheads at targets 1,500 kilometres away. Last Saturday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it has lifted its self-imposed 2,000km limit on the range of its ballistic missiles.

items.title: Trump may not attack Iran as long as it doesn't provoke US, report says
items.summary: Trump may not attack Iran as long as it doesn't provoke US, report says President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, according to three people familiar with the matter. Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes and winding down hostilities, and current and former officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind about how to resolve the unpopular conflict, which he launched in February with Israel. But in meetings with his national security advisers and after a series of intelligence briefings, Trump said he was considering holding off on strikes, said the people, who, like others interviewed for this story, spoke on condition of anonymity. He has also indicated sympathy for allies in the region who have asked him not to return to a full-fledged war. items.title: Iran's navy says three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.summary: Nov 14 (Reuters) - Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. One tanker hit a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, while two others struck mines later in the day. "Two violating tankers ... were attempting to slip through a prohibited route in the Strait of Hormuz when they hit naval mines, exploded, and burst into flames," Iran's IRNA news agency quoted the Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying about the evening incident.

items.summary: Iran’s IRGC says two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz Two oil tankers struck naval mines as they tried to cross the Strait of Hormuz “secretly”, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy says. In a statement published by Iran’s state news agency IRNA, the navy said the ships switched off their tracking and navigation equipment and took an “unauthorised” route. “Following the explosions of these two tankers, two other tankers that were attempting to transit secretly complied with the warnings from the Naval Force’s traffic control centre in the Strait of Hormuz and returned towards the waters of the Persian Gulf,” the IRGC said.

items.title: Iran’s IRGC denies role in French supermarket cyberattacks
items.summary: Iran’s IRGC denies role in French supermarket cyberattacks Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has rejected France’s accusation that an IRGC-linked cyber unit sabotaged supermarket refrigeration systems. The IRGC accused Israel of spreading misinformation. French authorities blame Shahid Kaveh for what they describe as the first large-scale cyber sabotage on French soil. On October 11 and 12, hackers drove temperatures inside refrigeration units to as high as 50C (122F) at about 700 stores. “Paris should beware the Zionist regime’s false flag trap,” IRGC spokesman Sardar Mohebi said on X. “Unlike the US and the Zionist regime, civilians have no place on the target list of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” he said, adding that the “ridiculous claim” is the “Zionists’ tired old playbook for stoking fear of Iran and winning allies in Europe”.

items.title: 'What would be left of international legal order': Araghchi on US strikes
items.summary: 'What would be left of international legal order': Araghchi on US strikes "If states were free to attack one another based on their own assessments of possible future threats, what would be left of the international legal order?" Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has asked in an opinion piece for Japan's Kyodo News. "This question," Araghchi wrote, "goes well beyond the political dispute between Iran and the United States." "It concerns one of the fundamental principles on which the international order established after the Second World War rests: the use of force is governed by law, and no state, however powerful, is entitled to place its own judgment above binding rules of international law," the article read. items.summary: US says it shot down two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain The US military on Friday said it had shot down two Iranian attack drones launched towards Bahrain, denying an Iranian claim that its forces had struck a US early-warning radar system in the Gulf kingdom. US Central Command (Centcom) said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain, both of which were intercepted by US forces. Centcom also rejected the IRGC’s claim that it had attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain earlier in the day. The competing accounts come amid questions from some US lawmakers about the Pentagon’s disclosure of details surrounding incidents in the conflict, while scepticism has also circulated on social media.

items.title: Snoh Aalegra: Legendary Love review – raw R&B talent restrained by reverence for the greats
items.summary: (Stem) Her truly remarkable, Sade-ish voice is hypnotic against some dizzyingly plush production, but a modern spin on 80s pastiche sometimes veers too close to tribute Swedish-Iranian singer Snoh Aalegra has previously described her music – a lush, pastiche-y mix of R&B, hip-hop, soul and pop – as “cinematic soul”. But although she’s a dab hand at graceful, timeless presentation (and has a truly remarkable voice) Aalegra’s music has often struggled to match up to its aesthetic, hampered by her love of the greats and a penchant for broadly generic lyrics. Her most recent album, 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies , made some headway toward carving out a more distinctive sound, thanks to sparky and inventive production from Tyler, the Creator, No ID, P2J and the Neptunes, but still didn’t quite feel like the right fit. items.title: Iran's Political Future and Prospects for Democracy
items.summary: Across Iran, women, workers, and ordinary citizens continue to challenge the Islamic Republic through protests, civil resistance, and defiance of government restrictions. Severe economic instability, international sanctions, and the costs of war have intensified pressure on the regime, raising concerns within its leadership about further domestic unrest. The prospect of a democratic Iran also raises fundamental questions about the country's nuclear ambitions, relations with Israel, and the future of regional security.

items.title: The Iran War: What Comes Next?
items.summary: Following two rounds of direct conflict with the United States and Israel, Iran has shifted its strategy from military confrontation to economic pressure through the Strait of Hormuz. While hardliners claim victory and seek greater regional influence, Iran faces severe inflation, a collapsing currency, and growing divisions within its leadership. With China playing an increasingly consequential role, the region faces competing visions of its future: economic cooperation and normalization or continued confrontation under Iran's regional ambitions.

items.title: Iran's Transformation: From US Ally to Adversary
items.summary: Iran's close ties with the United States and Israel once formed a cornerstone of American strategy in the Middle East. The 1979 Islamic Revolution marked a turning point, as the US embassy hostage crisis, economic sanctions, and the Islamic Republic's support for regional proxy groups deepened tensions with both countries. The regime's pursuit of nuclear capabilities and its opposition to secularism and religious pluralism further shaped its foreign policy and regional ambitions.

In a note to clients, Bank of America said Saudi Arabia is grappling with “contagion” caused by liquidity tightness in the UAE and a rapid slowdown in the kingdom’s own economy, according to an article published on Bloomberg on Tuesday. The report said Saudi banks are feeling the pain in the UAE, which is also grappling with fallout from the Iran war and tighter liquidity. Saudi banks are closely linked to their Emirati neighbours, with a high number of interbank transactions contributing to deposits at Saudi banks. At the same time, the Saudi economy is under strain and government entities are making withdrawals from Saudi banks. But loan demand is high, which is effectively raising the cost of Saudi money. items.title: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take  the decision to go to war seriously?
items.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. items.title: France supermarket hack marks new phase in Iran's shadow war
items.summary: The cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators that France has blamed on Iran marks a new phase in the asymmetric campaign Tehran is waging against the United States, extending it onto European soil, analysts say. Scores of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators, in some cases forcing them to throw away entire inventories of perishable food. France said Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind the "unprecedented" cyberattacks, a charge Iran rejected.

items.title: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?
items.summary: Unless you’ve been living under a rock (no shame Patrick Star!), you’ve likely heard about last Tuesday’s “Blue Wave” midterm elections . The Democrats’ strong performance at the polls flipped control of the House and the Senate, delivering stunning results on the way, including flipping long-time red states like Kansas and Texas. As the GOP scrambles to repair the damage and Democrats strategize about how to use their new power in a divided Washington, one takeaway seems obvious: this was a foreign policy election, in which the Iran war and the costs it brought home served as the tipping point. But can we read these election results as a repudiation of U.S. foreign policy writ-large, or is this a specific response to one of the dumbest interventions in the long history of American adventurism? What does JD Vance's day-after effort to distance himself from the war tell us about how Republicans are digesting this result? Israeli nuclear weapons, 2026
items.summary: Israel's longstanding policy of nuclear ambiguity ("amimut"), combined with severe intelligence restrictions and historical deception, continues to obscure the exact details of its undeclared nuclear arsenal. Despite these open-source research challenges, technical assessments suggest Israel maintains a strategic stockpile of roughly 90 single-stage, boosted fission warheads. This force is deployable across a triad of air, land, and sea delivery systems—including F-15/F-16/F-35 aircraft, Jericho ballistic missiles, and modified Dolphin-class submarines—even as US policy faces mounting domestic political pressure to abandon its decades-long refusal to acknowledge Israel's nuclear capability.

items.summary: Nov 10 (Reuters) - Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei said there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran and Washington, in an interview with pro-Iran broadcaster Al-Mayadeen. Iran has insisted the US must meet seven conditions set out in a June interim agreement before the Strait of Hormuz can reopen and negotiations resume. items.title: Cuts, evictions, and job losses: A view from the trenches of climate science in 2026
items.summary: A researcher at Columbia University who studies atmospheric and climate science gives a first-hand account of what it is like to pursue this work in the Trump 2.0 era, when the foundations of American science are being profoundly shaken. The post-World War II traditions that have made American science so successful—generous funding, awarded based on merit via peer review; academic freedom; openness to foreign talent; and most of all, systems of funding and executing science that are largely run by scientists, rather than by politicians—are under siege. What comes next is still an open question.

items.title: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security
items.summary: Water, energy, and mineral resources have long played a role in influencing and inciting political, ideological, and economic violence. But this violence is now worsening, driven by growing population pressures, expanding economies, and a fracturing and reforming of political alliances — and the wars in Ukraine, Israel-Palestine, and Iran. One surprising result may be an unanticipated acceleration of the global transition away from fossil fuels.

items.title: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality
items.summary: The historian Stephen Kotkin of Stanford’s Hoover Institution has penned an important new essay on the phenomenon of “junk history”: reductionist or plainly wrong interpretations of historical events that have little or no basis in empirical reality but are nevertheless “marshaled in policy debates as justification for action, up to launching wars.” The emblematic example, which has recently been used by advocates for the war with Iran, is the failure of British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain to truly ensure “peace in our time” at Munich in 1938. As Kotkin once put it, “It turns out not everything is Munich. It turns out Munich wasn’t even Munich when you get down into the nitty-gritty details.” Another example of junk history is what many otherwise well-informed American observers think they know about Sweden’s conduct during World War II and the Cold War. The figure rose from 48 percent in 2005 to 78 percent this spring, two-and-a-half years into the genocide in Gaza and just after Israel and the US had attacked Iran. In July, a YouGov opinion poll commissioned by the Council for British-Arab Understanding found that only 17 percent of the British population believes that Israel is not committing genocide in Gaza. items.title: El 'milagro' de dos centímetros que rescató a Amira: una historia de amor entre la medicina y la tecnología
items.summary: Hay historias que empiezan mucho antes de que nazca un niño. La de Amira comenzó cuando todavía era un pequeño corazón latiendo en el interior de su madre y los médicos descubrieron que algo no iba bien. El suyo latía demasiado despacio. Una bradicardia severa -frecuencia cardíaca muy baja- amenazaba con detener el reloj antes incluso de que la vida hubiera comenzado.Hoy Amira tiene ocho meses. Está viva. Y lleva dentro un dispositivo de apenas dos centímetros, el marcapasos más pequeño del mundo, diseñado específicamente para que un corazón tan diminuto como el suyo pueda seguir latiendo. Detrás de esos dos centímetros de tecnología hay meses de trabajo, una doctora que decidió llamar a una puerta que parecía demasiado grande para escucharla, doce ingenieros trabajando contra el reloj, y un científico de 65 años que decidió aplazar su jubilación para intentar salvar a una niña a la que no conocía.Es también, sobre todo, una historia de encuentros. Volgens het ministerie van Energie is de schade beperkt gebleven. Eerder meldden de Saudiërs dat ze twee raketten hadden onderschept die vanuit Jemen op Riyad waren afgevuurd door de Houthi's. Daarnaast zijn kruisraketten onderschept en vernietigd in het zuiden van Saudi-Arabië. The mass withdrawal of multinational corporations (MNCs) from Russia demonstrated that geopolitical risk had begun to outweigh the benefits of global economic interdependence. items.title: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers
items.summary: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers The United States Central Command (Centcom) has directed the establishment of a task force that will support US government's efforts to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials. In a statement issued on Saturday on X, Centcom said Admiral Brad Cooper has directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, an internal staff of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with other US government agencies on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and "illegal revenue streams" across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, Centcom added. "The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," said Cooper. items.title: US military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman
items.summary: US military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman A US military aircraft fired on and disabled a commercial vessel that tried to break the US naval blockade of Iran on Saturday, US Central Command (Centcom) said. The St Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo ship had visited an Iranian port and was trying to leave regional waters when a US plane fired precision munitions at its stern, after US forces ordered the crew to clear the targeted areas of the vessel, Centcom said. The US military also said on Saturday it was launching a task force to crack down on Iran’s movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material across its land borders and through the Caspian Sea, expanding on its months-long naval blockade. Centcom estimated that the blockade had prevented Iran from exporting more than $25bn worth of crude oil.

items.summary: Explosions reported on Iran's Qeshm Island and in port of Jask Explosions were heard on Saturday on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz and in the southern port of Jask, Iranian media reported, though there was no official confirmation of what caused them. The Iranian Tasnim news agency said earlier on Saturday that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, but did not say who fired them. There was no official word on damage. The reported explosions come days after US strikes on the island, which a US official described as limited and not a resumption of major combat operations.

items.summary: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards has said that it has lifted restrictions on the range of Iran's missiles. IRGC spokesman, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi reportedly made the comments at a press conference on Saturday, in response to question regarding the country's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei's warning to the US against further attacks on the country. Khamenei had previously said during a meeting with senior military commanders, that any renewed US or Israeli attck would be met with "with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response". The leader also reportedly ordered an update of Iran's military target database. According to Tasnim news agency, Mohebbi was asked on Saturday whether Khamenei's comments meant that limits on the range of Iranian missiles had been removed. He responded : "This restriction has been lifted for us". “Our duty is to show our capabilities on the battlefield,” he added.

items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. Iraanse staatsmedia melden op basis van getuigen dat twee projectielen zijn ingeslagen in het gebied Suza op het eiland Qeshm. Dat eiland ligt op een strategische positie in de Straat van Hormuz en herbergt belangrijke legerbases. Voorafgaand aan de inslagen was volgens de getuigen het geluid van een vliegtuig boven het eiland te horen. Er is nog niets bekend over schade. Wel stelt het Iraanse leger dat het een Amerikaanse MQ-9 Reaper, een drone, heeft neergeschoten boven Qeshm. 'Binnen een kwartier' Al enige tijd wordt ervan uitgegaan dat president Trump een omvangrijke, meerdaagse aanval op Iran voorbereidt. Hij zou dat over de verkiezingen hebben heengetild, in de hoop er niet op te worden afgerekend door de Amerikaanse kiezer. Desondanks leed zijn Republikeinse partij dinsdag een grote nederlaag . items.title: Iran will not allow US bases in the region to be rebuilt, army spokesman says
items.summary: Iran will not allow US bases in the region to be rebuilt, army spokesman says Iranian Army Spokesman Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia has said Iran's army will not allow US military bases in the region to be rebuilt. Akraminia said more than 228 locations or facilities at US bases across the region had been severely damaged or destroyed, according to Iran’s Fars news agency, claiming no US base in the region remained capable of operational missions, forcing US forces to bring in fuel for their vessels and supplies for personnel from outside the region. “We will never allow the enemy’s bases in the region to be rebuilt,” Akraminia said.

items.title: Europeans got blue blinders in wake of midterm sweep
items.summary: The Democratic sweep of the midterm elections has been greeted with a wary relief across Europe. After two years of President Donald Trump's tariffs, threats to annex Greenland and scolding of European NATO allies on defense spending, many European politicians see the Republican defeat as a welcome course correction. Yet the reactions also expose the contradictions of the European Union’s own foreign policy, particularly toward the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Rather than examining the causes of Trump’s defeat, EU leaders have chosen to interpret it as a vindication of their own ideological beliefs. The EU high representative for foreign policy, Kaja Kallas, unsurprisingly, saw in the election a hope that the new Congress will strengthen transatlantic unity and support for Ukraine, presumably reversing Trump’s insufficient devotion to the Ukrainian cause, which she criticized earlier. items.title: Freezer meltdowns and airline hoaxes are a taste of things to come. Hoping for the best is no longer an option | Elisabeth Braw
items.summary: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . items.title: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says
items.summary: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated than it was when the United States and Israel started the war in February, says Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia. "Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," Akraminia said, according to the state news agency Irna. "They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence." Akraminia said that Iranian armed forces retained control over the Strait of Hormuz and that it would remain closed until the United States accepted Tehran's demands. "Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
